title: 2005 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 7
statement: If \(a, b, c>0\), what is the smallest possible value of \(\left\lfloor\frac{a+b}{c}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{b+c}{a}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{c+a}{b}\right\rfloor\) ? (Note that \(\lfloor x\rfloor\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x\).)

solutions.text:
4
Since \(\lfloor x\rfloor>x-1\) for all \(x\), we have that

\[\begin{aligned}
\left\lfloor\frac{a+b}{c}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{b+c}{a}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{c+a}{b}\right\rfloor & >\frac{a+b}{c}+\frac{b+c}{a}+\frac{c+a}{b}-3 \\
& =\left(\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{a}\right)+\left(\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{b}\right)+\left(\frac{c}{a}+\frac{a}{c}\right)-3
\end{aligned}\]

But by the AM-GM inequality, each of the first three terms in the last line is at least 2. Therefore, the lefthand side is greater than \(2+2+2-3=3\). Since it is an integer, the smallest value it can be is therefore 4 . This is in fact attainable by letting \((a, b, c)=(6,8,9)\).
